items.description: An industrial hub located in Samdrup Jongkhar, designed to foster manufacturing and trade in eastern Bhutan.
A strategic industrial site in Samtse, focusing on diversifying the economy through manufacturing and processing industries.

The administrative center of Punakha District, famed as the site of the first king's coronation in 1907.
A popular Buddhist monastery dedicated to Drukpa Kunley, famous for its unique cultural symbolism.
A prominent landmark in Thimphu, built in honor of the third king to promote peace and prosperity.
One of the oldest fortresses in the country, built by Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal in 1629.
A historic fortress strategically built on a ridge to control trade routes between eastern and western Bhutan.
A fortress guarding eastern Bhutan, built on a cliff overlooking the Drangme Chhu and Gamri Chhu rivers.
A historic monastery in Thimphu, currently serving as a monastic school for young monks.
A sacred cliffside monastery complex clinging to the mountains above the Paro Valley, often called the Tiger's Nest.
A historic Buddhist university and monastery located north of Thimphu, known for its tranquil surroundings.
A beautiful temple in Phuentsholing representing the celestial abode of Guru Rinpoche.
A large white stupa in Trashiyangtse, inspired by the Boudhanath stupa in Nepal.
A serene monastic fortress perched on a hill above Punakha, offering panoramic views of the valley.
A protected area established to conserve the unique Himalayan ecosystem and biodiversity in western Bhutan.
